title: European-Chinese Smile mission begins science operations
excerpt: The spacecraft is now collecting data on how solar activity interacts with Earth's magnetic field.
bodyHtml:
The European Space Agency announced on 23 September that the European-Chinese Smile mission is ready to begin science operations. The spacecraft, which launched on 19 May and reached its target orbit on 20 June, has completed its in-space commissioning period.

During the commissioning phase, teams deployed mechanisms and tested the mission's four science instruments: the soft X-ray imager, ultraviolet aurora imager, magnetometer, and light ion analyser. These instruments are designed to study solar storms, geomagnetic storms, and space weather.

The mission is a joint project between the European Space Agency and the Chinese Academy of Sciences. The soft X-ray imager is expected to capture its first images of the magnetopause or the northern polar cusp by mid-October.
